tables.heading_path: Key Definitions
tables.caption: Key Definitions (Term, Definition)

body.t: Adolescents
Refers to people aged 10-19 years.
Associate

This refers to an approach led by HIV positive peer workers, who are trained to create and manage a “referral chain network”. Peer mobilizers have undergone HIV testing (and, if HIV positive, are enrolled in treatment); they pass referral slips for HIV testing to members of their social, sexual or drug networks.
Bidirectional referral
System considers both the information going from the health care system to the referred community program or resource
Children
Refers to people aged 0-9 years.
Community referral

This is a referral of a client made at community level by a Community Health care worker (Rural Health Motivators/ Community Expert Client/Community Mentor Mother) to the nearest health facility (clinic, health center, hospital).
Facility referral

This is a referral of a client made at health facility level by facility and health care workers within the same health facility (Intra-facility) or to another health facility (inter facility) for care that the health care workers do not have the capacity to provide.
Intra Facility
This is a referral made within different departments in the same health facility.
Inter facility
This is a referral made from one health facility to another health facility.
HIV index case
This is an individual diagnosed with HIV infection who draws attention to his/her sexual partner(s)/injecting drug users, biological children below 15 years and associates for HIV testing services.
HIV Self-testing
This is a process where an individual collects his or her specimen, performs a test and the results, often in a private setting, either alone or with someone he or she trusts.
Index contact
These are people who have had contact with the index case in a way which is associated with HIV transmission. It includes biological child(ren) <15 with an unknown status, partners, and associates.
Index case testing

This refers to an approach focused on testing individuals in the social or sexual networks of index cases, including children below the age of 15 years, sexual partners, needle-sharing partners, and other high-risk contacts. Index case testing describes the process of tracing and offering HIV testing services to the children, and partner(s) of both newly identified HIV infected individuals and those of already known HIV positive status; with a goal to identify those infected with HIV but are not aware of their infection or those with known HIV positive status not currently in HIV care.
Linkage to Care and Treatment

This is a process in which the client has reached the facility and provided with care and treatment services he/she needs. The referring facility verifies if the client has arrived and was provided with services, or the receiving facility gives feedback to the referring facility.
Linkage case management
Linkage case management (LCM) comprises the package of linkage services including individualized case management; treatment navigation and index testing.
Linkages Facilitator/ Linkage case management officer

This is a Health Care Worker who includes (Expert client, Mentor mother, Peer and Peer navigator) that is responsible for providing the package of evidence-based LCM services, enrolling HIV diagnosed client into ART care, and ensuring clients are retained on ART through their 2nd ART refill and ensure linkage to prevention services for clients that have tested negative.
National Referral form

This is a tool that is filled by health care workers (HCW) or community health care workers (CHW) when referring a client to another level of care to obtain care that is not provided at the initial level where help was sought.
Referral

This is the process of forwarding a client/patient to another service delivery point within the same health facility but different departments or to another health facility to get the possible care for that condition he/she has.
Active Referral: An active referral begins with assessment and prioritization of a client’s immediate needs for medical and/or risk-reduction services. In an active referral, a client is provided with assistance in accessing referral services, such as setting up an appointment, being escorted or given transportation cost/fee.
Passive Referral: In a passive referral, a client is provided with information, such as agency name and location, about one or more referral services. It is then up to the client to make decisions about whether and which services to access and how to access them.
Peer:

Person who belongs to the same age group or social group as someone else

A person with whom someone has had sex with. In the context of index testing, it refers to partner(s) one has had sexual contact with within the past 12 months.
Prevention package
Effective prevention interventions have been proven to reduce HIV transmission. Prevention packages include PREP, PEP, VMMC, Condom, HIVST, FP, STI
Stable clients
Clients that have tested HIV positive without opportunistic infections
Returning to Care
Any client that was once enrolled in ART returning after 28 days of treatment interruption
Delayed initiation
Clients not initiated on ART within 14 days of testing HIV positive

tables.heading_path: 5 Linkage to Treatment and Care > 5.4 Summary of Linkage case management services > Guiding Principles for Linkage Case Management
tables.caption: Guiding Principles for Linkage Case Management (1., LCM is voluntary; all eligible patients are free to enroll or discontinue services.)

header.t: LCM is voluntary; all eligible patients are free to enroll or discontinue services.

body.t: Quality and Inclusiveness; LCM should ensure that partners, family members, and associates of LCM clients are appropriately HIV diagnosed and linked to ART care.
Client centered: LCM should focus on the patient's client's concerns and priorities or must focus on problem solving approach to address concerns
Teamwork: Providers of LCM including clinicians, peers, lay staff, community workers, families, and the clients themselves should strive to always work together.
Transparency: Providers of LCM should ensure good communication at all stages of LCM implementation.

- Check any pending issues in the client chronic care file to be finalized
- Inform the client that this is the last visit.

- Remind the client that today they will be taken V/L and they will be called once the results are back. If the V/L is undetectable they will be enrolled into more intense DSD model. If the second one is still undetectable, they will then be transitioned into less intensive model

source_flags: Day 180: 'If the V/L is undetectable they will be enrolled into more intense DSD model. If the second one is still undetectable, they will then be transitioned into less intensive model' – an undetectable viral load leading to a MORE intensive model looks reversed.

For clients still not on ART at Day 180: 'Inform client that there is no need to test again, should they decide that they want to be initiated on ART' – conflicts with retesting for verification before ART initiation required elsewhere in the SOP (sections 9.3-9.5, 12.24, Annexure 1).

○ Health care worker who receives the client and verifies information in CMIS if the facility is on CMIS.
○ Must be aware of available referral services (both clinical services and community resources) at the preferred facility.
○ Provide the list for all sexual/ injecting partners, biological children below 15 years and associates.
○ If not already on ART conduct retesting for verification.
○ Must understand the services needed by the client.
○ Client should disclose to significant others, family, and partner when appropriate.
○ The facility must call the community health care worker (if client was not escorted) to update on client referral.
○ Initiate client on ART, give client two weeks supply
○ Client to honor appointments and adhere to treatment if initiated on ART
○ Document update in the referral form and file the referral slip.
○ Document referral form which include detailed physical address date client tested and HIV status or the services the client is being referred for.
○ Complete and return bottom referral slip to client to give to community health care workers.
○ Agree on the appointment date and the client's preferred facility.
○ Call the facility the client is being referred to make an appointment.

- Complete the referral form comprehensively and ensure the client is booked at the referred facility - Escort or meet clients at facilities and provide treatment navigation services for at least the first facility visit as per the need of the client. - Do follow up with receiving facility to confirm linkage of referred client. - Conduct at least one follow-up support calls before ART initiation (if not on the day of diagnosis), and two follow-up support call. - For Community partners implementing Community ART, clients must be initiated before being referred out. - Discuss with the client the importance of index testing and disclosure.

source_flags: Community initiation: 'give client two weeks supply' – consistent with the Day-14 first refill, but no instruction is given if the client does not link within the 7-day window while holding ART.

tables.heading_path: 3 Men
tables.caption: 3 Men (Children, Adolescents, Key populations, Men)

body.t:
○ For children below 5 years provide ART using family approach
○ For all children, the primary caregiver/ guardian is fully responsible for ensuring linkage and retention of the child.
○ Children depend on their parent's/ caregiver for linkages hence the importance and benefits of ART should be continuously. Emphasized on the parent/caregiver.

○ Establishing or reestablishing a peer support network (teen clubs) to provide physical and emotional care.
○ Above 12 years they can link to all health care services with the help of parents, caregiver, or treatment supporter of their own choice.
○ Emphasize on the importance and benefits of disclosure.
○ Provide Psychosocial support as per the need of the adolescent.

○ Provide outreach services that offer comprehensive HIV services.
○ Refer clients who are delaying ART initiation, missed appointment and those who disengaged from treatment to peer navigators to build social cohesion and participation.
○ Implementing index testing for sexual and/or drug injecting partners.

○ Provide IEC material on the benefits of early ART initiation.
○ Provide outreach services to male dominated industries that offer comprehensive HIV services.
○ If possible, assign male linkages facilitator who will provide empathetic guidance and support based on personnel experience as men diagnosed with HIV feels they alone.

- In situations where the child is denied care by the parent or caregiver the involvement of social workers is obligatory. - Educate parents/caregivers on the importance of age-appropriate disclosure - Use age-appropriate language in line with education and emotional readiness. - Use images or drawings to help children understand the explanations during counselling sessions. - Be honest. If you do not know the answer to the child's questions, say so.

- Provision of youth friendly service package (fast tracking adolescents in uniform, extension of hours, school holidays consideration and provision of comprehensive services) - Assess ART readiness and address barriers to ART initiation, and discuss benefits of ART, adherence, and retention. - Discuss importance of family planning for adolescents that are sexually active. - Discuss safer sex and risk reduction.

- If the HIV-positive client agrees, offer HIVST for \`secondary distribution. - Educate client on consistent use of condoms and lubricants with sexual partners. - Refer clients not ready to initiate according to the escalation plan.

- Provide men health days/ male friendly clinics (Provide extended hours or weekends for ART initiation, allowing clients to select preferred facility if there are issues of stigma.
- Enroll men into adherence club for men to support each other - STI screening at every visit and provide treatment if needed.
- Offer VMMC if client is eligible.
- Routine NCD screening - Assessment of risk factors for erectile dysfunction and premature ejaculation.
- Diabetes and anti-hypertensive drug refills

o Anticipate the impact of the disclosure on other family members, friends, the
o school and the community and plan for this.

o Promote the correct and consistent use of condoms among those who are sexually active and increase the uptake of STI screening and family planning services.
o Maintain privacy and confidentiality to reduce stigma and discrimination.
o Utilization of peer-to-peer counselling to share their personal experiences with anxiety, guilt, fear, shame, rejection, depression, and feelings of hopelessness for newly diagnosed adolescents.
o STI screening at every visit and provide treatment in necessary.
- Provision family planning to prevent unintended pregnancy. - Screen for breast and cervical cancer and link accordingly - For adolescent who have economic challenges refer them to community partners that can assist with economic empowerment

o Provision of curative services
o Discuss with the client what to do in case of travelling

tables.heading_path: 14 Annex > Barriers to ART Initiation
tables.caption: Barriers to ART initiation and possible interventions: individual factors (feeling well, no time, denial, stigma, substance use, lifelong commitment, side effects), interpersonal factors (lack of support, disclosure, traditional medicine, religion), health system factors (quality, hours, vertical services, staff attitude, unique identifier, queues, distance)

header.t: Client's perception for not starting treatment

body.t: 1. Feeling healthy/well (some men are unaware that early treatment can mean a longer and healthier life; some know but find it too …)
Client does not believe he/she needs to start treatment because of perceived good health. Patient argues that with a high CD4 count there is no need to start ART.

- Explain that the earlier an individual starts ART, the longer they can live without acquiring AIDS.
- Explain the goal of ART is to improve quality of life.
- Refer client to clinician for escalated counselling according to the facility-adapted plan.
- Clinician explains HIV progression using pre-treatment viral load.
- Inform client that treatment guidelines have changed and now nearly all clients can start ART on the day of diagnosis; explain the previous thresholds for starting ART (200-350-500).
2. No time; too busy with work, school or other responsibilities
Client believes he/she does not have time to initiate or come for refills.

- Enrol client on LCM.
- Explore the client's time commitments and underlying reasons.
- Provide motivational counselling.
- Develop a treatment plan that adjusts refill dates and times to suit the client.
- Appoint client for a counselling session at the agreed time and date.
- Inform client about DSD models once on treatment with an undetectable viral load.
- Refer client to clinician for escalated counselling.
3. Denies being HIV infected
Client believes he/she is not infected with HIV.

- Inform client that before ART initiation they will be retested for verification by another health care worker.
- Clinician explains HIV progression using pre-treatment viral load.
- Provide motivational counselling.
- Enrol client on LCM.
4. Loss of confidentiality and stigma
Client does not want others to know and fears stigmatisation if identified at the ART clinic.

- Explore why the client does not want others to know.
- Share benefits of disclosure and implications of not disclosing.
- Be cautious and explore the potential of partner violence.
- Explain the disclosure process.
- Inform client that ART services are now integrated into service points.
5. Substance abuse
Client has been drinking too much and/or using other drugs.

- Explain effects of substance abuse on adherence and possible interactions.
- Refer client to clinician.
6. Denial that client has HIV; wants confirmation in another facility
Client wants a second opinion.

- Clinician to refer client to psychologist / mental health nurse.
- Complete referral form and empower client to produce it at the site wherever he/she tests.
- Inform client that before ART initiation they will be retested for verification by another health care worker, within or in another facility of his/her choosing.
7. Concerned about lifelong commitment
Client is worried that he/she might not be able to adhere to treatment.

- Demystify ART (explain what it is, how it works and potential side effects).
- Enrol client on LCM.
- Yes, ART is lifelong treatment, and it is not the only one: there are other conditions that need treatment for life, e.g. diabetes, hypertension.
8. Fear of side effects
Client is concerned about side effects.

- Inform the client that there are simpler, less toxic combinations.
- Inform clients about possible side effects and advise them to report to a nurse or doctor as soon as possible.
- Encourage treatment ownership and reporting of new or unfamiliar symptoms at each visit.
- Explain the continuous monitoring of side effects by the clinician during refills, which has scaled up early identification of side effects.
1. Fears lack of support, violence, or separation from spouse/partner, or partner's disapproval
Client fears they might not get support from close family members, partner(s), peers and associates.

- Educate client on the disclosure process (who, why, when and how).
- Explain benefits of disclosing status.
- Refer client to social worker for further counselling and support.
- Encourage client to join a support group for peer support.
2. Wants to disclose to partner first
Fears the partner's reaction if they start treatment; perceived lack of support from spouse if he/she starts ART; lacks skills to disclose.

- Educate client on the disclosure process (who, why, when and how).
- Explore the reasons why the client wants to disclose to the partner before initiation.
- Refer client to social worker / mental health nurse / psychologist for further counselling and support.
- Refer to the 101 counselling job aid.
3. Believes in traditional medicine
Client believes that traditional medicine cures HIV or AIDS.

- Explain the basic facts about HIV.
- Inform client of possible drug interactions with traditional medicine.
- Refer for further counselling as per escalation plan.
4. Has strong religious beliefs
Client believes that prayer will cure HIV or AIDS.

- Explain the basic facts about HIV.
- Refer for further counselling as per escalation plan.
1. Quality or delivery of HIV care is poor
Client believes treatment offered is sub-standard.

- Ascertain why the client thinks services offered are sub-standard.
- Inform clients that there are standard trainings for all HCWs in the country.
- Document referral to the preferred site and set an appointment.
- Enrol into LCM for follow-up.
2. Operational hours not conducive to clients
Facility operating hours.

- Explore a possible time for initiation.
- Inform client about DSD models offered by the facility that can suit his/her situation.
- Facility should develop a plan on how to manage clients unable to attend during normal operating hours.
3. Vertical ART services
Clients feel vertical ART services will lead to incidental disclosure.
Inform client that ART services are now integrated into service points.
4. Health care worker's attitude towards clients
Clients feel they have been mistreated.

- Inform clients of the procedure for reporting mistreatment.
- Assure the client that the facility will support them and has the best intention for all clients.
- Explain that the earlier an individual starts ART, the longer they can live without acquiring AIDS.
5. Use of unique identifier
Clients perceive that there would be a breach of confidentiality.
Explain why it is necessary to use a unique identifier.
6. Long queues at facilities
Client thinks he/she does not have enough time to wait in line.
Inform client about the DSD model once on treatment with an undetectable viral load.
7. Long distance to health facility
Client believes ART can only be initiated at certain health facilities.

- Initiating ART at community level.
- Assure the client that ART has been decentralised to most health facilities in the country.

source_flags: Individual factor 1: the barrier cell ends mid-sentence ('Some know but find it too').
Individual factor 1 asks the clinician to explain the old CD4 thresholds for starting ART (200-350-500); this may confuse clients now that treatment starts at diagnosis.
Health-system factor 4 (staff attitude) includes 'explain that the earlier an individual starts ART the longer they can live', which seems misplaced from factor 1.
tables.context_before: Assess and resolve (if applicable) enrolment barriers for all clients, and before case closure be sure all barriers have been resolved; if not, refer according to the facility escalation plan. Objective: to help clients overcome ART initiation barriers and retain them in care using the LCM strategy.

tables.heading_path: 14 Annex > 14.1 Annexure 1 Linkages for Client Testing Positive in the Facility
tables.caption: Annexure 1. Linkages for a client testing HIV positive in the facility: true new positive verification (CMIS/APMR), RTT package, readiness assessment, retesting, ART initiation, LCM enrolment
tables.content:
1. Tested HIV positive → true new positive verification (CMIS, APMR).
2a. Found in any of the information systems → provide the RTT (return to treatment) package: welcome the client, support, do not be judgmental, review last treatment, refer client for counselling → readiness assessment.
2b. Not found in any information system → readiness assessment.
3. Ready → retesting for verification as per the HTS algorithm → initiate ART as per ART initiation guidelines → enrol into LCM → offer prevention package (e.g. TPT, CaCx) → follow the client as per LCM guidance to ensure retention.
4. Not ready → enrol into LCM; escalation counselling (doctor, nurse, social worker, HTS provider, expert client, psychologist) → follow the client as per LCM guidance until initiation → offer prevention package (TPT, CaCx) → follow as per LCM guidance to ensure retention.
source_flags: The flowchart prints 'CMIS.APMAR'; elsewhere the system is 'APMR'.

tables.heading_path: 14 Annex > 14.2 Annexure 2 Linkages for Client Returning to Care
tables.caption: Annexure 2. Linkages for a client returning to care by interruption type: missed appointment (<28 days), early interrupters (28 days-6 months), late interrupters (>6 months) – RTT package, enhanced adherence counselling, escalation
tables.content:
HIV positive → verify previous HIV-positive / ART registration in any system (CMIS, APMR) – found in system:
- Missed appointment and defaulter (immediate interrupters, <28 days post initiation) → offer relevant prevention services according to client's preferences → enrol client into LCM.
- Interruption in treatment (LTFU), early interrupters (>28 days up to 6 months post initiation) → provide RTT package → enhanced adherence counselling.
- Interruption in treatment (LTFU), late interrupters (>6 months on ART) → provide RTT package → counsel client based on EAC for late interrupters guidelines to ascertain barriers → escalate client based on needs after ascertaining barriers.
source_flags: For clients on ART who missed an appointment (<28 days), the chart says 'offer relevant prevention services according to client's preferences' rather than resuming ART/adherence support; probably copied from the HIV-negative pathway.
Early interrupters are defined by time 'post initiation' and late interrupters by time 'on ART'; the categories overlap for someone who interrupted more than 6 months after starting ART.
